judged_text: updateEvent's fallback branch evaluates `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the predicate compares every calendar's externalId against undefined, never matches, and selectedCalendar resolves to undefined instead of the previous `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Updates/reschedules of bookings whose calendar reference lacks externalCalendarId (legacy references, or references created by the no-credentialId create path where result.externalId is undefined) now pass calendarId: undefined to calendar.events.update — the call fails instead of targeting the destination calendar, so the Google event keeps the old slot while the booking is rescheduled.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, the fallback branch is now:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (null/undefined), the `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId === undefined`, so it will not select the intended destination calendar (e.g., the first/"main host" calendar). This is a regression from the previous behavior (`: event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`) and will produce `selectedCalendar === undefined` even when `event.destinationCalendar` is populated, causing the subsequent `calendar.events.update` to target no calendar id (or a wrong default depending on how `calendarId` is later used). The same flawed pattern appears in `deleteEvent` as well.
